title: Petal Hush — Clean Beauty Pedestal
description: A single serum bottle rests on a soft disc pedestal against a pale blush ground, anchored by a whisper-thin oval wordmark and a vertical lowercase ingredient column — restraint used as a brand statement rather than decoration.
philosophy: This template exists for products whose packaging is the entire argument. It refuses hard shadows, competing copy blocks, and any layout tension that might dilute the bottle's presence. The silence is intentional: the kind of trust that Glossier and Tatcha built came not from shouting but from the confidence to leave space empty. It is designed for brands that believe softness and legibility are the same virtue.
goodFor: Hero product launch slides for skincare or wellness DTC brands
Ingredient transparency 'what's inside' feature moments in a brand deck
Brand pitch decks with a clean-beauty or minimalist positioning section
Single-SKU product reveal adapted from an Instagram-native visual language
avoidFor: Multi-product catalog or side-by-side comparison layouts
Chart-heavy quarterly business or sales performance reviews
B2B SaaS or enterprise technology product presentations
High-contrast conference keynote openers that must read at 30 feet
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the first breath inside a Japanese apothecary — still, luminous, and unhurried. A single product form commands the center with ceremonial calm, the background a barely-there blush that glows rather than saturates. Compositional rhythm is radially quiet: all supporting elements recede inward so the product can hold its silence without competition. Avoid shadow drama, graphic flourishes, layered textures, or any copy hierarchy that introduces tension; the only contrast is between the soft pedestal's gentle mass and the open air surrounding it.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; the product-on-pedestal is centered across cols 4–9, staged just above vertical center to create an elevated, ceremonial showcase quality. Outer margins breathe at roughly 10%, forming a contained stage with no bleed tension — the whitespace IS the frame. The wordmark sits centered below the pedestal in a narrow horizontal band, its oval enclosure suggested purely by surrounding negative space rather than a drawn rule. A vertical lowercase column anchors flush to the right edge in cols 11–12, running nearly full height as a quiet typographic spine that whispers rather than announces.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like opening a brand's ingredient pamphlet tucked inside tissue paper — unhurried, confident, and slightly ceremonial. Composition is deliberately asymmetric: a quiet column of copy on the left breathes against an airy organic shape on the right that holds either a product detail or a soft pedestal echo. The mood is transparency as luxury, the kind of restraint that signals the brand has nothing to hide and no need to shout. Avoid clinical list density, hard geometric framing, and any element that creates visual tension competing with the central stillness.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with content running as a lowercase vertical column in cols 2–4 and a soft disc or oval shape anchoring the visual zone in cols 7–11. Outer margins breathe at roughly 8–9% of slide width; no header band, no rule lines. Hierarchy is carried by scale contrast between a small label line and its entry text, with a hairline dot as the only decorative punctuation. Page marker sits bottom-right, flush to the outer margin.
